unspecified.behavior: Two different .loft files that point to the same YouTube video id share the no-retry guard when one embed instance moves between them. After the first file's API load failed, the second file shows the link card without a new load attempt.

scores.reason: It needs two .loft files for the same video played one after the other in the same embed instance, right after a transient script failure. The user sees the link card, not a blank box.

The reported behavior exists in the code. YouTubeEmbed.tsx:127-130 keys failedVideoIdRef on videoId only, and the effect at :266-267 returns early when the video id matches. So if the IFrame API load failed (rare: offline or a script blocker) and the user then goes straight to a second .loft of the same video without a remount, that file shows the link card from the earlier failure (loadFailed stays true) and no new load is tried, even though loadYouTubeIframeApi.ts:69-74 resets the cache so a retry could work; the user still gets a working link and a reload fixes it.

unspecified.behavior: When LoftPlayer's fileId changes, the old file's content stays rendered until the new .loft fetch resolves. In that window the embed gets the new fileId together with the old URL, so a player for the previous video can briefly be bound to the new file's progress tracking.

scores.reason: Moving between two .loft files in place keeps the previous video on screen for the short fetch window on a LAN; the 5-second progress threshold makes a wrong progress write unlikely.
